notes.definition: Plants produce hormones to coordinate and control growth and their responses to light (phototropism) and gravity (gravitropism or geotropism). Unequal distribution of the hormone auxin causes unequal growth rates in shoots and roots, making them bend.
explanation: Plants cannot move around, but they can change the direction in which they grow. A tropism is a growth response towards or away from a stimulus. Phototropism is a response to light: shoots grow towards light so their leaves can absorb more light for photosynthesis. Gravitropism (also called geotropism) is a response to gravity: roots grow downwards, in the direction of gravity, and shoots grow upwards, against gravity. Roots growing down anchor the plant and reach water and mineral ions.

These responses are controlled by the plant hormone auxin, which is made in the tips of shoots and roots and moves down through the plant. Unequal distributions of auxin cause unequal growth rates. In shoots, auxin stimulates cell elongation (cells get longer). In roots, auxin inhibits cell elongation.

Phototropism in a shoot: when light comes from one side, auxin moves to the shaded side of the shoot. The cells on the shaded side elongate more than the cells on the lit side. The shaded side grows faster, so the shoot bends towards the light. When the shoot points straight at the light, auxin becomes evenly spread again and the shoot grows straight.

Gravitropism: if a seedling is placed on its side, gravity makes auxin collect on the lower side of both the shoot and the root. In the shoot, the extra auxin stimulates elongation on the lower side, so the shoot bends upwards. In the root, the extra auxin inhibits elongation on the lower side, so the upper side grows faster and the root bends downwards.
Higher tier: other plant hormones are also important. Gibberellins are important in initiating seed germination. Ethene is a gas that controls cell division and the ripening of fruits.

Required practical 8: you can investigate the effect of light or gravity on the growth of newly germinated seedlings. For example, cress seedlings on damp cotton wool are put in a light-proof box with a slit so light comes from one side, while a control group has light from all directions. Or seedlings are placed on their side in the dark. Measure the length of seedlings or the angle of bending each day with a ruler or protractor, keeping temperature, water and seed type the same.
keyFacts: Plant hormones coordinate and control growth and responses to light and gravity.
Phototropism is a growth response to light; shoots grow towards light.
Gravitropism (geotropism) is a growth response to gravity; roots grow down, shoots grow up.
Auxin is made in shoot and root tips.
Unequal distribution of auxin causes unequal growth rates.
In shoots, auxin stimulates cell elongation; in roots, it inhibits cell elongation.
Light from one side: auxin moves to the shaded side, which grows faster, so the shoot bends towards light.
On their side: auxin collects on the lower side; shoots bend up and roots bend down.
Higher: gibberellins are important in initiating seed germination.
Higher: ethene controls cell division and the ripening of fruits.

keyTerms.definition: A plant growth response to light. Shoots show positive phototropism (grow towards light).
A plant growth response to gravity. Roots grow in the direction of gravity; shoots grow against it.
A plant hormone made in shoot and root tips that controls growth by affecting cell elongation.
Cells getting longer, which makes a plant part grow in length.
Higher tier: plant hormones important in initiating seed germination.
Higher tier: a gaseous plant hormone that controls cell division and the ripening of fruits.
A directional growth response of a plant to a stimulus.

workedExamples.title: Mean growth rate of seedlings
workedExamples.question: A cress seedling is 8 mm long on day 0 and 29 mm long on day 7. Calculate its mean growth rate.
steps: Mean growth rate = 21 ÷ 7 = 3 mm per day

workedExamples.title: Dealing with an anomalous result
workedExamples.question: Five seedlings in one-sided light bent by 34°, 36°, 35°, 58° and 33°. Calculate the mean angle, ignoring any anomalous result.
steps: 58° is much larger than the others, so it is anomalous and is left out.

workedExamples.title: Unit conversion: comparing cell lengths
workedExamples.question: A cell on the shaded side of a shoot is 0.15 mm long. A cell on the lit side is 100 μm long. How many times longer is the shaded-side cell?
steps: Convert to the same unit: 0.15 mm × 1000 = 150 μm
workedExamples.answer: 1.5 times longer, because more auxin on the shaded side causes more cell elongation.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think auxin moves towards the light.
misconceptions.right: In fact auxin moves to the shaded side of the shoot. That side grows faster, which bends the shoot towards the light.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think auxin has the same effect in roots and shoots.
misconceptions.right: In fact auxin stimulates cell elongation in shoots but inhibits it in roots, which is why they bend in opposite directions.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the shoot bends because cells on the lit side shrink or die.
misconceptions.right: In fact both sides grow, but cells on the shaded side elongate more.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think plants bend towards light by moving, like animals.
misconceptions.right: In fact tropisms are growth responses: the bending is caused by unequal growth, so it is slow and permanent.

realWorld: House plants on a windowsill bend towards the window, so gardeners turn them regularly to keep them growing straight.
Seeds sown upside down still produce roots that grow down and shoots that grow up, because of gravitropism.
Understanding these hormones led to their commercial use, such as rooting powders and controlled ripening of fruit (see Uses of plant hormones).
higherTier: Gibberellins are important in initiating seed germination.
Ethene controls cell division and the ripening of fruits.
separateOnlyContent: This whole subtopic, including required practical 8 (effect of light or gravity on newly germinated seedlings), is assessed only in separate Biology (8461), not in Combined Science Trilogy.
examTips: Use precise wording: auxin moves to the SHADED side, causing MORE CELL ELONGATION there. 'Auxin makes the plant grow' is too vague.
Remember the root/shoot difference: auxin stimulates elongation in shoots but inhibits it in roots.

In practical questions, name the independent variable (direction of light or position relative to gravity), the dependent variable (length or angle) and control variables (temperature, water, seed type, light intensity).
Exclude anomalous results before calculating a mean, and say why you excluded them.
Gibberellins (germination) and ethene (cell division and ripening) are Higher tier only.
summary: Plant hormones control growth responses to light and gravity.
Shoots: positive phototropism, negative gravitropism. Roots: positive gravitropism.
Auxin is unequally distributed by one-sided light or gravity, causing unequal growth.
Auxin stimulates elongation in shoots but inhibits it in roots.
Higher: gibberellins initiate germination; ethene controls cell division and fruit ripening.
Required practical 8 investigates light or gravity on seedling growth.

A plant growth response to gravity; roots grow down, shoots grow up.

flashcards.front: Which hormone controls phototropism and gravitropism?

flashcards.back: In the tips of shoots and roots.

flashcards.front: Where does auxin go when light comes from one side?
flashcards.back: To the shaded side of the shoot.

flashcards.front: Why does a shoot bend towards light?
flashcards.back: More auxin on the shaded side makes cells there elongate more, so that side grows faster.

flashcards.front: Why does a horizontal root bend down?
flashcards.back: Auxin collects on the lower side and inhibits elongation, so the upper side grows faster.

flashcards.back: Leaves absorb more light for photosynthesis.
Controls cell division and ripening of fruits.
Independent: direction of light (or gravity). Dependent: seedling length or angle of growth.

questions.question: What is the name of a plant's growth response to light?
markScheme: 1 mark: Phototropism
questions.explanation: 'Photo' means light and 'tropism' means a growth response. Gravitropism is the response to gravity. Photosynthesis and transpiration are processes, not growth responses.

questions.question: Which plant hormone controls phototropism?
markScheme: 1 mark: Auxin
questions.explanation: Auxin controls growth responses to light and gravity. Ethene controls ripening, gibberellins germination, and insulin is an animal hormone.

questions.question: In which direction do plant shoots grow in response to light?
options: They do not respond to light
markScheme: 1 mark: Towards the light
questions.explanation: Shoots show positive phototropism, which lets leaves absorb more light for photosynthesis.

questions.question: How do plant roots respond to gravity?
options: They grow downwards in the direction of gravity
markScheme: 1 mark: They grow downwards in the direction of gravity
questions.explanation: Roots show positive gravitropism. This anchors the plant and helps roots reach water and mineral ions.

options: It makes cells on the lit side divide faster
It increases the rate of photosynthesis
markScheme: 1 mark: It stimulates cell elongation
questions.explanation: In shoots auxin makes cells get longer. In roots auxin has the opposite effect and inhibits elongation.

The lower side grows faster, so the root bends upwards
Both sides grow at the same rate, so the root stays horizontal
markScheme: 1 mark: The lower side grows more slowly, so the root bends downwards
questions.explanation: In roots auxin inhibits cell elongation. The upper side, with less auxin, grows faster, so the root curves down.

questions.question: What is the main role of gibberellins in plants?
options: Causing shoots to bend towards light
markScheme: 1 mark: Initiating seed germination
questions.explanation: Gibberellins are important in starting seed germination. Ripening is controlled by ethene; bending towards light by auxin.

questions.question: Which processes in plants are controlled by ethene?
options: Cell division and ripening of fruits
markScheme: 1 mark: Cell division and ripening of fruits
questions.explanation: Ethene is a gaseous plant hormone. The specification states it controls cell division and the ripening of fruits.

options: The number of seeds in each dish
markScheme: 1 mark: The direction of the light
questions.explanation: The independent variable is the one the student changes. Seedling length (or angle) is the dependent variable. Number of seeds and temperature should be controlled.

questions.question: Give the meaning of the terms phototropism and gravitropism.
markScheme: 1 mark: phototropism is a growth response to light
1 mark: gravitropism / geotropism is a growth response to gravity
questions.explanation: Both are tropisms: directional growth responses. Saying 'movement' instead of 'growth' is not credited.

questions.question: Give one advantage to a plant of its shoots growing towards light.
markScheme: 1 mark: leaves absorb more light for photosynthesis
questions.explanation: More photosynthesis means more glucose for respiration and growth.

questions.question: Explain how a plant shoot bends towards light that comes from one side.
markScheme: 1 mark: auxin moves to the shaded side of the shoot
1 mark: auxin stimulates cell elongation / cells on the shaded side elongate more
1 mark: the shaded side grows faster, so the shoot bends towards the light
questions.explanation: The three marking points form a chain: auxin redistribution, more elongation, unequal growth causing bending.

questions.question: Explain why it is an advantage for roots to grow downwards.
markScheme: 1 mark: to anchor the plant in the soil
1 mark: to reach water and mineral ions
questions.explanation: Water is needed for photosynthesis and support; mineral ions (such as nitrate) are needed for healthy growth.

questions.question:
A bean seedling is placed horizontally.
Explain why its root grows downwards.
markScheme: 1 mark: (due to gravity) auxin collects on the lower side of the root
1 mark: in roots auxin inhibits cell elongation
1 mark: so the upper side grows faster and the root bends downwards
questions.explanation: The key difference from shoots is that auxin inhibits elongation in roots. Many students lose a mark by saying auxin makes the lower side grow faster.

questions.question: A student investigates the effect of light direction on the growth of cress seedlings. Give two variables the student should control.
markScheme: 1 mark each, any two: temperature; volume of water added; type/species of seed; age of seedlings; light intensity; number of seeds per dish
questions.explanation: Controlling these variables means only the direction of light affects how the seedlings grow, making it a fair test.

questions.question:
A student grows cress seedlings in light that comes from one side only.
Describe how the student could measure the effect of the light on the seedlings.
markScheme: 1 mark: measure the length of each seedling with a ruler (in mm) or the angle of bending with a protractor
1 mark: at regular intervals / each day, and calculate a mean for each group
questions.explanation: Measuring several seedlings and calculating a mean reduces the effect of individual variation.

questions.question:
A seed is kept in conditions where it cannot produce gibberellins.
Suggest what would happen to the seed.
Give a reason for your answer.
markScheme: 1 mark: the seed would not germinate (or germination would be delayed)
1 mark: because gibberellins are needed to initiate seed germination
questions.explanation: Gibberellins start germination, so without them the seed stays dormant even if water, oxygen and warmth are available.

questions.question:
In an investigation, cress seeds are grown on damp cotton wool in a Petri dish with a lid.
Suggest why the cotton wool is kept damp and why a lid is used.
markScheme: 1 mark: seeds need water to germinate and grow
1 mark: the lid reduces evaporation so the cotton wool does not dry out (keeping water a controlled variable)
questions.explanation: If some dishes dried out, water availability rather than light would affect growth, making the test unfair.

questions.question:
A student measured the lengths of five cress seedlings.
Table 1 shows the results.
Calculate the mean length of the seedlings.
markScheme: 1 mark: 70 ÷ 5 = 14 mm
questions.explanation: Add the five lengths and divide by 5.

questions.question:
A cell on the shaded side of a shoot is 0.15 mm long.
A cell on the lit side of the same shoot is 100 μm long.
Calculate how many times longer the cell on the shaded side is than the cell on the lit side.
markScheme: 1 mark: 0.15 mm = 150 μm
questions.explanation: Convert to the same unit first: 1 mm = 1000 μm. The cell on the shaded side is longer because it received more auxin, which stimulates elongation in shoots.

questions.question:
Five seedlings were grown in light from one side.
Table 1 shows the angle each seedling bent towards the light.
Calculate the mean angle of bending.
Do not include the anomalous result in your calculation.
markScheme: 1 mark: identifies 58° as anomalous and excludes it
questions.explanation: 58° does not fit the pattern of the other results. Including it gives 39.2°, which is not representative.

questions.question:
Describe a method to investigate the effect of light from one side on the growth of newly germinated seedlings.
Your method should give valid results.
markScheme: Indicative content: place the same number of seeds of the same type (e.g. cress) on damp cotton wool in two Petri dishes; allow them to germinate in the same conditions; place one dish in a light-proof box with a slit so light comes from one side only; place the control dish in light from all directions (or in a box with no slit); keep temperature, water volume and light intensity the same; measure the length of each seedling with a ruler or the angle of bending with a protractor each day for several days; record results in a table; calculate the mean; compare the direction and amount of growth between groups; repeat the investigation.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): coherent method that would produce valid results, with a control group, at least two control variables and a clear measurement method.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): method with some detail of set-up and measurement; may lack a control group or control variables.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): basic steps such as putting seedlings near a light.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: A good method can be followed by someone else. Include the control group, what is kept the same, what is measured, how and how often.

questions.question:
A seedling is placed on its side in the dark.
After two days, its shoot has grown upwards and its root has grown downwards.
Explain these observations.
markScheme: Indicative content: auxin is made in the tips of the shoot and root; gravity causes auxin to collect on the lower side of both the shoot and root; this is an example of gravitropism / geotropism; in the shoot, auxin stimulates cell elongation; cells on the lower side of the shoot elongate more; the lower side grows faster, so the shoot bends upwards; in the root, auxin inhibits cell elongation; cells on the lower side of the root elongate less; the upper side grows faster, so the root bends downwards; the dark ensures light does not affect growth (no phototropism).
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): full explanation of auxin distribution and its opposite effects in shoot and root, leading clearly to the directions of growth.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): explanation for either the shoot or the root, or both with some errors.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements, e.g. auxin moves due to gravity, or roots grow down.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Level 3 requires the contrast between shoots (auxin stimulates) and roots (auxin inhibits). Always link auxin concentration to cell elongation and then to the direction of bending.

questions.question: Describe the roles of the plant hormones auxin, gibberellins and ethene.
markScheme: Indicative content: auxin controls growth responses to light (phototropism) and gravity (gravitropism); unequal distribution of auxin causes unequal growth rates; auxin stimulates cell elongation in shoots and inhibits it in roots; gibberellins are important in initiating seed germination; ethene controls cell division; ethene controls the ripening of fruits.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): correct role of all three hormones, with some detail for auxin.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): correct role for one or two hormones.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Gibberellins and ethene are Higher tier content. Learn one key phrase for each: germination for gibberellins, ripening and cell division for ethene.
